description.narrative: This investment consolidates Australia's regional funding assistance to improve health outcomes in the Pacific. Support is provided through key multilateral and regional partners, including the Pacific Community’s Public Health Division, the Royal Australasian College of Surgeons, Fiji National University’s College of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences and the United Nations Children's Fund. Activities under this investment support: specialised clinical services; research; health systems strengthening; non-communicable disease prevention and control; and the training of healthcare workers.

Evaluation of The Pacific Community (SPC) Public Health Division (PHD) Investments

description.narrative: Australia, through the Pacific Community’s Public Health Division (SPC PHD), supported Pacific Island Countries and Territories to strengthen their communicable diseases surveillance, preparedness, management and response. For example, in 2023 through this investment, 99 participants (26 male, 73 female) received Post-Graduate Certificate in Field Epidemiology (PGCFE). As a result, participants have strengthened capacity to support national and local-level management of communicable diseases.

In 2024, Australia strengthened the research capacity of the Fiji National University (FNU) to help build Fiji’s capacity to combat priority pathogens. With this support, FNU facilitated training for 29 participants and established a serology laboratory to undertake the Population-Based Age-Stratified Assessment of SARS-CoV2 Seropositivity in Fiji (PASS Fiji) project. The PASS Fiji study concluded that three years after the pandemic, Fiji still demonstrated high immunity to SARS-CoV2 (>99%) and two variants of concern (delta 95.9% and omicron 98%). FNU worked with the Fiji Ministry of Health and Medical Services (MHMS) and community leaders to share these findings with communities that were part of the study. Early feedback indicates increased trust in MHMS and vaccine safety by communities.

This umbrella investment ($31m 2021-28) consolidates Australia's regional funding assistance to improve health outcomes in the Pacific by strengthening health systems through the areas of specialised clinical services, research, service delivery, communicable and non-communicable diseases, health workforce improvement, basic healthcare, and health information systems. In 2022, Australia’s support enabled Fiji National University to design and commence the first COVID-19 vaccination impact research in the Pacific called the ”Population based age-stratified assessment of SARS-CoV-2 seropositivity in Fiji” to help guide ongoing COVID-19 vaccination strategies and strengthen Fiji’s teaching and research capability through the procurement and installation of its own serology laboratory.
